from_quote: On the nearest-neighbor lattice Z^d, d>=2, suppose every edge weight lies in [a,b] with 0<a<=b<3a. Between any adjacent vertices x,y the unique geodesic is the direct edge, so its maximum distance from [x,y] is zero. In particular, D(0,e_1)=0 and inf_{v!=0} E D(0,v)/|v|^s=0 for every real s. This does not address an asymptotic lower bound restricted to sufficiently large |v|.
to_quote: INVALID INFERENCE: a positive bounded iid weight law such as Uniform[1,2] automatically satisfies the lower wandering condition in Auffinger-Damron (2014), printed equation (2.2). That condition takes the infimum of E D(0,v)/|v|^s over every nonzero displacement; a zero-deviation neighboring geodesic makes the infimum zero. Chatterjee (2013) A4 instead only requires the condition outside a sufficiently large ball.
rationale: The adjacent-edge geodesic has D(0,e_1)=0 for Uniform[1,2], so that law fails the literally printed all-v lower wandering premise.

to_quote: Auffinger and Damron (2014), Theorem 2.2, prove chi=2xi-1 for iid nonnegative nearest-neighbor edge weights on Z^d, d>=2, when the law has mass below p_c(d) at the infimum of its support and the global strong exponents in their (2.1)-(2.2) satisfy chi_a=chi_b and xi_a=xi_b. The proof does not require the nearly-Gamma assumption. Theorem 2.1 is their new proof of the <= inequality; combining it with the previously known >= inequality gives their Theorem 2.2. No passage-time law is proved in that paper to satisfy the matched-exponent premise. Their printed (2.2) lower bound takes an infimum over every nonzero displacement, unlike Chatterjee (2013) A3-A4, which exclude a finite ball.
rationale: The source-audit gate records the all-nonzero-v quantifier in (2.2); the adjacent-edge lemma shows why that precise quantifier matters.
